coverage.r1: First 6 min are English (app demo). Medi's Arabic is Latin-transliterated through ~37:00, Arabic script after; two 'Unclear - needs audio review' Medi turns (01:51, 02:24). Amal's Arabic is garbled in places (08:57 'سعود' for صوروا, 10:14 'وحم' for حمس, 43:07 'سيفاء' for عاصفة). Left out as S4 pronunciation: 10:17 'ams' for حمّس (dropped ح), 25:12 inti maz'ooj self-fixed to maz'ooja, 33:44 biniz'aj 'ej sound', 34:54 baz'ajni->biz'ajni self-fix then 'almost', 35:57/36:31 ta'az'aj letter-order slips (she asked 'which goes first, ز or ع'), 49:57-51:28 'matanzajini' for don't annoy me which Amal treated as over-stressed ع (ما تزعجيني), 55:16 شبعان heard as 'hot'. Self-fixes skipped: 44:28 بزعج->بنزعج, 54:52 bansabit->بنبسط, 58:22 أتعبك->أتعبها, 59:18 باتعب->أتعب after لما (B3). 45:27 Amal 'Been catching you saying the [?] instead of the ب' - target word inaudible, no row. 32:06 'shu ra7ty' unclear, Amal 'شو تحكي؟'. 29:25 za'ajatek vs her أزعجتك: she said learn both variants, not filed. Amal ruled at 53:49 that إذا keeps the b- (إذا بكون), which conflicts with buckets.md B3.
coverage.r2: Lines 1-140 (00:26-06:10) are English app talk, no Arabic from Medi. Medi's Arabic is Latin-transliterated from 06:17 to ~36:48, Arabic script from ~36:48 to 45:20, then mixed. Amal's Arabic is sometimes garbled by the engine (08:57 'سعود' for صوروا, 43:07/43:29 'سيفاء' for عاصفة, 31:06 'أزعجتُ' for أزعجتوه, 36:44 'زد أن دنع'). Not written (S4 pronunciation / root-letter slips): 'bisbat' for bibsit [13:28] and her B-S-T order note [21:01]; 'wa atik' for وقتك [08:01]; 'oo ams' for وحمس [10:17]; 'biniz'aj' vowel note [33:54]; 'matanzajini' stretch 50:10-51:28 which she treated as ع stress; 'Azajitini' [52:00]; 'شبعان' heard as hot [55:23]; 'إيه' for هي [57:49, 59:13]; 'joan' for جوعان. Not written (self-fixed before she helped): 'inta baz'aj' -> bitz'aj [33:05], 'بزعج، بنزعج' [44:28], 'ana bansabit' -> بنبسط [54:52], 'باتعب' -> أتعب after لما [59:18], 'هي انزعج' -> انزعجت [41:17]. Medi's 'shu ra7ty' [32:06] is unclear (she answered شو تحكي؟). Medi's 'khalee' [09:37] was accepted as possible but not wanted. Meta questions in English (futtuli [17:54], adverb [24:15], 'does this take من' [42:06]) not written.

r3_note: Lesson = review of ببسط/بنبسط then the new pair بزعج/بنزعج (drill-heavy, Medi's Arabic mostly in Latin letters until ~37:00, Arabic script after). D2 and D9 are the same moment (10:10-10:17, C9); kept once as D2. D1's real substance is not خلّى but انبسط written for بسط at 09:55-10:04 (B12) - merger: make sure that row is in the agreed set, otherwise add it. Two let-pass/fixed slips I could not see in the disputes and cannot tell from the agreed set (NOT added, please check): (a) 49:06 'matanzajini' (ما تنزعجيني) for 'don't get annoyed by me' - Amal said 'No' at 49:21 and modelled ما تنزعجي مني (verb takes من, not an object suffix; D2/D4); (b) 10:38 'nafs?' offered for 'everyone' when she asked 'what's everyone?' - she gave الكل (vocab-A tier 1 or tier 0 asked). D13/D14 are the same slip on the masculine then the feminine negative command 30 s apart; kept as two rows because she corrected each separately - fold if the merger treats immediate repeats as one.

rows.medi_said: Okay, so isn't it en-enbistee? Did you enjoy? ... Oh, I put enbustee.
rows.amal_said: انبسطتي. ... Yes, it is double T. You forgot the double T and the في.
rows.why: He dropped the past-tense -t- before the -i ending (enbustee); she recast انبسطتي and said 'it is double T, you forgot the double T'.

rows.medi_said: I put enbustee (no في)
rows.amal_said: But what is it-- what is missing? It's not "انبسطتي." Something is missing. What is it? ... "في" or be?
rows.why: انبسط takes في/ب before its object (enjoy your time = انبسطتي في وقتك); he left the preposition out and she prompted until he said 'the fee'.
rows.english: Did you enjoy your time outside?

rows.medi_said: Yeah, enbasat, didn't I?
rows.amal_said: You put "انبسط". ... does the تخيل have emotions? Does it get happy?
rows.why: He used انبسط (get happy) where the subject (camping) makes others happy, so it must be بسّط; she prompted 'does camping have emotions?' and he fixed 'this is without the B... el takheem basat'.

rows.medi_said: el takheem basat kul hadha oo ams.
rows.amal_said: حم. بسط وحمس. Let's put the verbs together.
rows.why: For 'camping made everyone happy and excited' he split the two verbs around the object (basat kul hada oo [h]ammas, second verb left dangling); she recast بسط وحمّس and said 'Let's put the verbs together' [10:30], then supplied الكل for everyone [10:40]. 'ams' is the transcriber's garble of حمّس.
rows.english: Camping made everyone happy and excited.
rows.r3_why: Both readers saw this; the matcher missed it because r1 used 10:10 and r2 10:17 (his line is split across two transcript lines). Kept once here; D9 is dropped as the duplicate.

rows.medi_said: nafs?
rows.amal_said: كل حدا or what's everyone? ... الكل.
rows.why: Asked for 'everyone' he offered nafs (self/same), a different word; she supplied الكل. Sheet row: 'all / everyone | Elkul | الكل' (she then also accepted his كل حدا).

rows.medi_said: Is it, isn't it lisa ma bansabit?
rows.amal_said: This is I don't get happy yet. What about don't get happy? It's a command. ... Command, so we keep the... ما تنبسط لسه.
rows.why: 'Don't get happy yet' is a negative command (ما + you-form تنبسط); he gave a negated present ma bansabit (I don't get happy); she named it a command and he reached ma teenbesit.

rows.medi_said: Ma teenbesit lisa ma ba'arif kul shey.
rows.amal_said: Ma, we don't know.
rows.why: The subject is 'we' but he conjugated for 'I' (ba'arif); she prompted 'we don't know' and he fixed to ma ben a'arif.
rows.english: Don't get happy yet, we don't know everything

rows.medi_said: Is that the same? Andesit ishish?
rows.amal_said: انبسطت؟ ... إي.
rows.why: 'Enjoy something' needs the preposition (انبسطت بإشي); he attached the object directly, she echoed انبسطت؟ and he added 'be'.

rows.medi_said: Imbare lele or lele imbare
rows.amal_said: ليلة امبارح.
rows.why: 'Last night' is an idafa: ليلة first, امبارح second, and the feminine first word grows -t (lelet imbare); he tried owner-first and then lele imbare without the -t; she recast ليلة امبارح and he produced lelet imbare.

rows.medi_said: and anbisit, anbisit hafla- haflatik.
rows.amal_said: Mm-mm. We forgot something. ... في ... حفلتك.
rows.why: انبسط needs في/ب before the object; he said anbisit haflatik with no preposition, she said 'we forgot something' and he added fi.

rows.medi_said: Okay. So ma'tanbisti halak.
rows.amal_said: Mm-mm. I'm gonna keep making you repeat until you say في on your own. ما تنبسط بحالك. That's في or ب.
rows.why: Same missing preposition (انبسط في/ب): ma tanbisti halak lacks fi/b before halak; she refused it until he said fi halak and recast ما تنبسط بحالك.

rows.medi_said: And I don't know how to say too much, right?
rows.amal_said: You can say كتير. كتير or extra. ... زيادة.
rows.why: He said he did not know 'too much'; she supplied كتير (sheet: 'a lot / very / much | Kteer | كتير'); his 'extra' guess Ziyada was right.

rows.medi_said: so anbisti fi laylak.
rows.amal_said: This your night. One night. ... بليلتك. Yes. ليلتك.
rows.why: ليلة is feminine so 'your night' is ليلتك (the -t comes back before the ending); he said laylak; she prompted 'your night, one night' and he fixed laylatik.

rows.medi_said: so I, I think I remembered mazuj as annoying and moza- mozaj as annoyed.
rows.amal_said: بالعكس. If it has this oo sound. مزعوج، موجوع، محروج، مجروح. All of them is annoyed. Feeling the thing, not causing it.
rows.wrong: mazuj as annoying and moza- mozaj as annoyed
rows.right: مزعوج = annoyed (feeling it), مزعج = annoying (causing it)
rows.why: Asked 'which is which?' [22:54] he swapped the two participles; she said بالعكس and then named the pattern rule (oo pattern مفعول = feeling it, short pattern = causing it, later 'same pattern as مزعج: متعب' [24:05]). Filed as grammar B15 rather than vocab tier 1 because her fix is the participle pattern, exactly as بسط/انبسط is B12 not vocab; sheet rows 46-47 (annoyed | Maz3ooj | مزعوج; annoying | Muz3ej | مزعج) show both words are hers.
rows.english: I remembered maz'ooj as annoying and muz'ej as annoyed (wrong way round).
rows.r3_why: Same slip in both readers; only the label differed. The transcript supports grammar B15: she corrected with the pattern rule, not by supplying a different lexical item.

rows.medi_said: Mutab? ... No.
rows.amal_said: Do you remember متعب؟ ... is tiring. Same pattern as مزعج.
rows.why: Didn't-know: asked if he remembered متعب he said no and she supplied the meaning (sheet: 'tiring | Mut3eb | متعب').

rows.medi_said: "hadhol el swat."
rows.amal_said: الأصوات.
rows.why: Plural of صوت is أصوات; he said swat with the initial أ missing, she recast الأصوات; may be only pronunciation (dropped hamza) rather than a plural-pattern slip.

rows.medi_said: You guys annoy him. Why is that my favorite? Az'aj, az'ajtu.
rows.amal_said: أزعجتُ. You can't say أزعجتُ، wo. ... Yes, there is an h.
rows.why: 'You (pl) annoyed him' needs the object ending on the verb (أزعجتوه); he stopped at az'ajtu; she said you can't say that and pointed to the h at the end.

rows.medi_said: don't want to annoy them. Ana ma, ma bitti, az'ajkum.
rows.amal_said: أزعجهم.
rows.why: 'Them' is the ending -hum, not -kum (you pl); he said az'ajkum, she recast أزعجهم.
rows.english: I don't want to annoy them

rows.medi_said: So, hadha al-jaw, annoys me. Baz- baz'ajni. Ana biyaz...
rows.amal_said: يعني almost. صح. بيزعجني.
rows.why: Subject is 'this weather' (3rd m.) but he put the 1st-person prefix ba- (baz'ajni = I annoy me); she said 'almost' and modelled بيزعجني [35:09, 35:17], he repeated biz'ajni. He had started to repair ('biz-' [35:08]) but the fix was completed with her model, so not a clean self-fix.
rows.r3_why: Real subject-agreement slip with a voiced recast; medium because his own repair overlapped hers.

rows.medi_said: So, don't annoy me. Ma ta'az-- Ma ta-- Ma ta'az'ajni. Ma ta'az'aj.
rows.amal_said: Which goes first؟ الـ ز أو الـ ع؟ ... ممتاز. ما تزعجني.
rows.why: He built the negative command on the past stem أزعج (ma ta-'az'aj, an extra a-/ع syllable before ز) instead of the bare you-form تزعج; she prompted 'which goes first, ز or ع?' until he reached 'ma tiz'ajni' [36:22] and she confirmed ما تزعجني [36:30]. The ز/ع ordering itself borders on S4, but the extra syllable is a stem-formation error.
rows.r3_why: Only r2 wrote it; transcript shows a genuine prompt-then-fix on the negative command form.

rows.medi_said: ma ta'az'ajini. Ma ta'az'ajini.
rows.amal_said: ما تزعجيني. ... تزعجيني. ... ✓ Yes. ما تزعجيني.
rows.why: Same extra a-/ع syllable on the feminine negative command right after he had said the masculine correctly [36:22]; she recast ما تزعجيني at 36:35 and 36:44, he repeated it wrong twice [36:36, 36:42] and got it at 36:48. Low because the relapse seconds after a correct masculine form may be articulation (S4) rather than the rule; merger may fold into D13 as a repeat.
rows.english: Don't annoy me (said to a woman).
rows.r3_why: Real correction sequence, but likely a repeat of D13 and possibly articulatory; kept low so the merger can decide.

rows.medi_said: So الولاد أزعجووو، أزعجووو،
rows.amal_said: أزعجوه؟
rows.why: 'Did the kids annoy him' needs the him-ending -h on أزعجوا; he stretched the -uu with no ه and she recast أزعجوه؟ (he still said أزعجو after).

rows.medi_said: هو بيزعج، بيزعجوني.
rows.amal_said: بيزعج، ... بيزعجني.
rows.why: Subject is هو (he) but he put the plural ending -u on the verb (بيزعجوني = they annoy me); she recast بيزعجني and he repeated it.

rows.medi_said: Okay, so بي-بيزعج-بيزعجوني.
rows.amal_said: بزعجني.
rows.why: Same slip a minute later for 'it annoys me': plural -u on a singular subject; she recast بزعجني and he asked 'why do I have the o in there?'.

rows.medi_said: انزعجتم. انزعج، انزعجنا.
rows.why: Levantine you(pl) past ending is -tu (انزعجتو), not the MSA -tum he used; she let it pass while he ran the conjugation.

rows.medi_said: Well, God. أنا نسيت الكلمة. أنا نسيت الكلمة.
rows.amal_said: سيفاء. [transcript garble of عاصفة]
rows.why: Didn't-know: he said he forgot the word for storm and she supplied it (he echoed عاصفة [43:09]); sheet row 1400: storm | 3aasefe | عاصفة.

rows.medi_said: إحنا بنن-بننزعج.
rows.amal_said: بننزعج. ... Been catching you saying the [letter inaudible in transcript] instead of the ب.
rows.why: She recast بننزعج [45:20] and told him she has been catching him using another letter instead of the ب on the we-form [45:27]; he accepted ('Oh, I didn't... بننزعج' [45:36]). Real by her words, but the transcript normalises his form to بننزعج and drops the letter she named, so the slip itself cannot be quoted - kept low per brief, nothing invented.
rows.r3_why: Her correction is explicit in the transcript; his wrong form is not visible, so low confidence rather than drop.

rows.medi_said: ليش، ليش فرق من-- ليش فرق من WhatsApp? ... ليش فرق؟
rows.why: 'Why is it different from WhatsApp' wants the adjective مختلف (sheet row 235: different (from) | mu5talef | مختلف) or غير; فرق is the noun 'difference' - a different lexical item, so tier 1 not tier 2 (tier 2 would be a wrong form of the same word). She only said كيف؟ [46:05], he repeated in English and she answered without fixing it. Best reading, B. (Secondary: من where مختلف takes عن.)
rows.english: Why is it different from WhatsApp?
rows.r3_why: Both readers agree it is a let-pass vocab error; tier 1 fits because فرق and مختلف are different words, not two forms of one word.

rows.medi_said: Oh, oh, oh, okay. تستعمل الـ-- يتستعمل الـ telephone.
rows.why: Restating her 'عم بستعمل الـ telephone' back to her as 'you use the phone' he dropped the b- and the feminine -i (تستعمل); she just went on ('آه، لأنه الـ computer خربان'). Low: casual echo and 'يتستعمل' shows the transcriber struggled with the line. 'telephone' is her own word here and is not on the sheet, so no tier-3 vocab.
rows.r3_why: Plausible let-pass b-drop in a form the transcript actually shows; kept low for Amal's review page rather than dropped.

rows.medi_said: ما تزع-- ما تزعجي. ما تزع-- ما، ما تن-- Oh yeah, that's right. ما تنزعج. ما تنزعج.
rows.amal_said: تنزعجي. ... ما تنزعجي. Cuz it's ززز، all of them together. ... ما تنزعجي. خلص.
rows.why: For 'don't get annoyed' he dropped the ن and produced ما تزعجي (don't annoy); she recast ما تنزعجي at 48:13 and 48:33 until he said it [48:39].

rows.medi_said: Don't be annoyed. Don't get annoyed by me. So this is without the N.
rows.amal_said: ليش؟ ... ليش؟
rows.right: with the N: ما تنزعجي (مني) - the get-annoyed verb انزعج
rows.why: For 'don't get annoyed by me' he picked the make-verb stem (زعج, 'without the N') instead of the get-verb انزعج; she prompted ليش؟ twice [48:57, 49:00] until he said 'you're right, it does have an N' [49:06]. Stated in English but it is a make-X vs get-X choice in the Arabic he was about to build.
rows.r3_why: Real: she withheld the answer and prompted until he fixed the stem choice; not a self-fix since the ليش came first.

rows.medi_said: It does have an N. ma-matan, matanzajini.
rows.amal_said: No. ... By me. ما تنزعجي. ... Yes. ما تنزعجي مني. كمان مرة.
rows.why: انزعج is intransitive: 'by me' is من + ending (مني), not an object ending -ni on the verb; she said No and gave ما تنزعجي مني, he repeated matanzaji minni.

rows.medi_said: Anabazaj. Na ba-banj.
rows.amal_said: Gets.
rows.why: 'I get annoyed' is the N-verb بنزعج; he said bazaj (I annoy); she prompted 'gets' and he fixed anabanzaj.

rows.medi_said: Yeah, anabanzaj, lama...
rows.amal_said: If.
rows.why: The sentence was 'if I'm hungry'; he started the clause with لما (when) instead of إذا; she said 'If' and he fixed Iza.

rows.medi_said: Oh, if. Iza. Iza akoon joan.
rows.amal_said: بس إذا بكون، مش أكون. ليش؟ ... If is conditional، but it doesn't take out the be. It keeps it.
rows.why: Her ruling: after إذا the ykoon form keeps its b- (إذا بكون), he dropped it (akoon); he fixed iza bakoon. Note this contradicts buckets.md B3 which lists iza among b-drop words - Amal's rule wins.
rows.english: I get annoyed if I'm hungry

rows.medi_said: أنا بزعج مين
rows.amal_said: mean or what's the better one؟ The one who. يلي.
rows.why: 'I annoy who(ever) annoys me' needs the relative اللي/يلي, not the question word مين; she prompted 'the one who' and he said اللي.

rows.medi_said: اللي who annoys me. Okay. So، اه، بينزعجني.
rows.amal_said: ليش أن annoys me. ... ✓ mm-hmm.
rows.why: 'annoys me' is the make-verb بيزعجني; he used the get-verb with an object (بينزعجني); she asked 'ليش أن? annoys me' and he fixed بيزعجني.

rows.medi_said: إيه بتنزع، بتنزعج لما I make retired.
rows.amal_said: Her. ... ✓ Yes، أتعبها.
rows.why: Arabic-led sentence (هي بتنزعج لما ...) with the last verb phrase dropped in English though the verb is on her sheet (row 821: i tire / make people tired | Ana bata33eb | بتعِّب); after a 30 s stall she prompted 'Her.' and he produced أتعب ... أتعبها [58:22], which she confirmed. The English piece stands for one Arabic word, so not the 'whole clause is English' exclusion. r2's أتعبك -> أتعبها at 58:22 is his own fix inside the same turn before any help, so it is not a separate row.
rows.english: She gets annoyed when I make her tired.
rows.r3_why: The two readers wrote two different pieces of one moment; the transcript supports the English drop-in (r1) as the error she prompted on, while the -ك/-ها slip was self-repaired in the same breath (S: self-fix before help).

rows.medi_said: annoyed. أنا انزعجت.
rows.amal_said: I didn't get.
rows.why: 'I wasn't annoyed' needs ما before the verb; he said the affirmative أنا انزعجت; she prompted 'I didn't get' and he fixed أنا ما انزعجت.

rows.medi_said: اه، أنا، اه، زعلان. ... زعلان، زعلان.
rows.amal_said: زعلت. ... Here's your inter-internal flip. زعلت. ... أنا ما انزعجت، أنا زعلت.
rows.why: For 'I was sad' (past, parallel to ما انزعجت) he used the present-state adjective زعلان with no past marker; she recast the past verb زعلت three times. Sheet rows 1164 (Za3laan) and 675 (Ana baz3al).

rows.medi_said: تعال. bye.
rows.why: Signing off he said تعال (come here) where a goodbye (يلا / سلام / بشوفك) fits; may be a transcription slip; Amal only said Bye. Best reading marked as B.
